source-fda-p000009.title: Implantable defibrillation
source-fda-p000009.purpose: An implantable defibrillator for selected patients at high risk of sudden death from ventricular arrhythmias, including survivors of cardiac arrest or poorly tolerated sustained ventricular tachycardia.
source-fda-p000009.relevance: The indication concerns the heart’s ventricular rhythm. It does not establish a brain interface or a vagus-nerve implant.
source-fda-p000009.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010015.title: Biventricular pacing for heart failure
source-fda-p010015.purpose: A biventricular pacing system for patients with moderate to severe heart failure who remain symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy and meet the original electrical-conduction and ejection-fraction criteria.
source-fda-p010015.relevance: The pulse generator and cardiac leads support pacing of the heart; the approval does not specify a precise generator location here.
source-fda-p010015.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010030.title: Wearable cardiac defibrillation
source-fda-p010030.purpose: A wearable cardioverter defibrillator for adults at risk of sudden cardiac arrest who cannot receive or refuse an implantable defibrillator, under the original indication.
source-fda-p010030.relevance: The intended treatment concerns cardiac rhythm. The system is wearable; this is not evidence of implantation inside the heart.
source-fda-p010030.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p060040.title: Mechanical support before heart transplantation
source-fda-p060040.purpose: A left ventricular assist system originally indicated as a bridge to transplantation for transplant candidates at risk of imminent death from irreversible left ventricular failure.
source-fda-p060040.relevance: The assisted structure is the heart’s left ventricle. This original approval does not describe every later destination-therapy indication.
source-fda-p060040.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100045.title: Wireless pulmonary-artery pressure monitoring
source-fda-p100045.purpose: Wirelessly measures pulmonary-artery pressure and heart rate to inform heart-failure management. The original indication covered NYHA class III patients hospitalized for heart failure in the previous year.
source-fda-p100045.relevance: The measured vessel is the pulmonary artery; the clinical purpose is heart-failure management. This is not a sensor implanted in lung tissue.
source-fda-p100045.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p150033.title: Leadless cardiac pacing
source-fda-p150033.purpose: Provides pacing for specified symptomatic conduction disorders, including selected high-grade AV block and sinus-node dysfunction cases. The original indication includes situations where atrial lead placement is difficult, risky or unnecessary.
source-fda-p150033.relevance: The intervention addresses cardiac electrical rhythm. Eligibility depends on the exact rhythm disorder; this summary does not assign an intracardiac coordinate.
source-fda-p150033.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100009.title: Catheter-based reduction of mitral regurgitation
source-fda-p100009.purpose: A percutaneous intervention to reduce significant symptomatic degenerative mitral regurgitation in patients judged at prohibitive surgical risk by a heart team, under the original indication.
source-fda-p100009.relevance: The treated structure is the mitral valve. This entry concerns valve repair, not replacement of the aorta or a coronary artery.
source-fda-p100009.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000037.title: Mechanical aortic valve replacement
source-fda-p000037.purpose: Replaces a diseased, damaged or malfunctioning native or prosthetic valve in the aortic position, in the approved sizes.
source-fda-p000037.relevance: The target is the aortic heart valve. The word aortic does not make this a separate treatment of the aortic vessel wall.
source-fda-p000037.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p020047.title: Coronary stenting to widen narrowed vessels
source-fda-p020047.purpose: Stents intended to improve coronary lumen diameter in specified native coronary lesions, bypass-graft lesions and acute myocardial-infarction presentations. The original approval defines lesion length and vessel-size limits.
source-fda-p020047.relevance: The source explicitly identifies coronary arteries and certain bypass grafts. The exact lesion and access route are not located on this reference model.
source-fda-p020047.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p110010.title: Drug-eluting coronary stenting
source-fda-p110010.purpose: An everolimus-eluting coronary stent intended to improve lumen diameter in symptomatic ischemic heart disease with specified de novo native coronary lesions, subject to the original lesion and vessel criteria.
source-fda-p110010.relevance: The treated vessels are coronary arteries. This is neither a cardiac pacing lead nor evidence of clinical superiority over another stent.
source-fda-p110010.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p020004.title: Endovascular exclusion of an abdominal aneurysm
source-fda-p020004.purpose: A stent-graft intended to exclude an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm from circulation in patients whose aortic neck, iliac landing zones and vascular access satisfy the original anatomical requirements.
source-fda-p020004.relevance: The treatment site is the abdominal aorta. Iliac and femoral access requirements are delivery constraints, not separate therapeutic targets in this entry.
source-fda-p020004.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100040.title: Thoracic aortic aneurysm repair
source-fda-p100040.purpose: An endovascular stent-graft for specified thoracic aortic aneurysms and penetrating ulcers in patients with suitable access and landing-zone anatomy.
source-fda-p100040.relevance: The treated vessel is the thoracic aorta. The regional diagram does not establish an individual patient’s graft position or suitability.
source-fda-p100040.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p030047.title: Carotid stenting with embolic protection
source-fda-p030047.purpose: Used with the AngioGuard emboli-capture guidewire for carotid revascularization in selected patients at high risk from endarterectomy. The original indication specifies symptomatic or asymptomatic stenosis thresholds and vessel sizes.
source-fda-p030047.relevance: The source identifies the common or internal carotid artery. This does not imply implantation in brain tissue.
source-fda-p030047.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010003.title: Adjunctive sealing during large-vessel repair
source-fda-p010003.purpose: An adjunct to sutures, staples and other standard methods of achieving hemostasis during open repair of large vessels in adults.
source-fda-p010003.relevance: The source explicitly names the aorta and carotid arteries among the large vessels. The adhesive supplements surgical closure; it is not an intravascular stent.
source-fda-p010003.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100022.title: Drug-eluting femoropopliteal stenting
source-fda-p100022.purpose: A drug-eluting stent intended to improve lumen diameter in symptomatic de novo or restenotic lesions of above-knee femoropopliteal arteries, within the original diameter and lesion-length limits.
source-fda-p100022.relevance: The intervention targets leg arteries, not the knee joint itself. Above-the-knee describes vessel location, not a knee prosthesis.
source-fda-p100022.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p080032.title: Bronchial thermoplasty for severe asthma
source-fda-p080032.purpose: A bronchial thermoplasty system originally indicated for adults with severe persistent asthma not well controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta agonists.
source-fda-p080032.relevance: The relevant anatomy is the bronchial airway within the lungs. This indication does not establish benefit for all asthma severities.
source-fda-p080032.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p160013.title: Preserving donor lungs outside the body
source-fda-p160013.purpose: Preserves standard-criteria donor lungs in a ventilated, perfused, near-physiologic state for double-lung transplantation, under the original indication.
source-fda-p160013.relevance: The system operates on donor lungs outside the recipient. It should not be read as a permanently implanted breathing device.
source-fda-p160013.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p180002.title: Bronchoscopic valve treatment for emphysema
source-fda-p180002.purpose: An implantable bronchial valve for adults with hyperinflation associated with severe emphysema in lung regions with little to no collateral ventilation.
source-fda-p180002.relevance: The source identifies bronchial placement and affected lung regions. This is a lung intervention, not replacement of a pulmonary heart valve.
source-fda-p180002.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p080030.title: Glaucoma pressure reduction during cataract surgery
source-fda-p080030.purpose: Used with cataract surgery to reduce intraocular pressure in adults with mild to moderate open-angle glaucoma already treated with ocular hypotensive medication, under the original indication.
source-fda-p080030.relevance: The treated function is pressure regulation within the eye. Cataract surgery is the co-procedure; it does not make this stent a lens replacement.
source-fda-p080030.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000030.title: Optical correction with soft contact lenses
source-fda-p000030.purpose: Soft contact lenses for correction of myopia or hyperopia in non-diseased eyes, within the original astigmatism limit. The historical approval specifies wear, replacement and disinfection requirements.
source-fda-p000030.relevance: These are external optical lenses associated with the corneal surface, not surgically implanted intraocular lenses. Wear instructions depend on the applicable labeling.
source-fda-p000030.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010018.title: Temporary correction of farsightedness
source-fda-p010018.purpose: A refractive treatment for temporary reduction of specified spherical hyperopia in patients aged 40 or older with stable refraction. The original approval states that the correction diminishes over time.
source-fda-p010018.relevance: The context is corneal refractive treatment. It should not be presented as permanent correction or as lens replacement.
source-fda-p010018.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000046.title: Maintaining space and protecting tissues during eye surgery
source-fda-p000046.purpose: A sodium-hyaluronate surgical aid that maintains chamber depth and visibility and protects intraocular tissues during specified operations, including lens implantation, corneal transplantation and retinal reattachment.
source-fda-p000046.relevance: The original statement explicitly names procedures involving cornea, lens and retina. This is a surgical aid, not a retinal electrode or an optical implant.
source-fda-p000046.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010059.title: Stabilizing the lens capsule during cataract surgery
source-fda-p010059.purpose: Stabilizes the crystalline-lens capsule in adults with weak or partially absent zonules undergoing cataract extraction with intraocular-lens implantation.
source-fda-p010059.relevance: The supported structure is the lens capsule and its support apparatus. The ring supports the capsule; it does not itself provide optical lens power.
source-fda-p010059.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p030002.title: Intraocular lens implantation after cataract removal
source-fda-p030002.purpose: An intraocular lens implanted in the capsular bag to correct aphakia after cataractous-lens removal in adults. The original approval describes intended near, intermediate and distance vision.
source-fda-p030002.relevance: The implant replaces the optical function of the removed lens. This is distinct from a contact lens worn on the eye’s surface.
source-fda-p030002.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000025.title: Cochlear electrical stimulation for hearing loss
source-fda-p000025.purpose: Intended to provide auditory information through electrical stimulation of the auditory nerve in specified severe-to-profound hearing-loss populations who gain little benefit from conventional amplification.
source-fda-p000025.relevance: The entry concerns the cochlear auditory pathway. The original approval includes different adult and pediatric hearing and hearing-aid-trial criteria.
source-fda-p000025.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p090018.title: Fully implanted hearing assistance
source-fda-p090018.purpose: An implantable hearing system intended to alleviate hearing loss by replicating the ossicular chain and adding gain, for patients meeting the original hearing and anatomical requirements.
source-fda-p090018.relevance: The source concerns mechanical hearing transmission in the ear. It is not an intracortical recording system or a cochlear-nerve electrode.
source-fda-p090018.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000023.title: Temporomandibular joint reconstruction
source-fda-p000023.purpose: Reconstructs the temporomandibular joint in specified conditions such as refractory inflammatory arthritis, recurrent ankylosis or failed prior reconstruction.
source-fda-p000023.relevance: The temporomandibular joint connects the mandible and skull. This is jaw-joint reconstruction, not a tooth filling or brain implant.
source-fda-p000023.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p040013.title: Regenerative treatment of periodontal defects
source-fda-p040013.purpose: A growth-factor enhanced matrix for specified intrabony and furcation periodontal defects and gingival recession associated with periodontal defects.
source-fda-p040013.relevance: The relevant tissues support teeth and include periodontal bone and gingiva. This is not a general-purpose bone graft for every skeletal region.
source-fda-p040013.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p170029.title: Imaging active tooth demineralization
source-fda-p170029.purpose: Provides images of active demineralization on accessible coronal tooth surfaces to aid assessment, diagnosis and treatment planning for caries-related lesions in patients aged six or older.
source-fda-p170029.relevance: The measured surface is the tooth crown. The device aids dental assessment; an image alone is not proof of a treatment outcome.
source-fda-p170029.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100049.title: Reflux management when medical therapy is insufficient
source-fda-p100049.purpose: An anti-reflux implant for patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease confirmed by abnormal pH testing who remain symptomatic despite maximum reflux therapy, under the original indication.
source-fda-p100049.relevance: The clinical target is reflux at the gastroesophageal junction. This is not a stomach-removal procedure, and the regional association does not establish exact placement.
source-fda-p100049.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000008.title: Adjustable gastric banding for severe obesity
source-fda-p000008.purpose: A gastric-banding intervention originally indicated for severely obese adults who failed conservative weight-loss approaches and met specified weight or BMI criteria. Long-term eating-habit changes are part of the original indication.
source-fda-p000008.relevance: The intervention concerns the stomach. It is not a treatment placed in the pancreas, despite its potential relationship to metabolic disease.
source-fda-p000008.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p110015.title: Measuring gastric emptying through breath analysis
source-fda-p110015.purpose: Uses a test meal and the carbon-isotope ratio in breath to measure solid gastric-emptying rate and aid diagnosis of delayed emptying in symptomatic adults, under professional supervision.
source-fda-p110015.relevance: The physiological function being measured is stomach emptying. The analyzer measures breath outside the body; no sensor is implanted in the stomach.
source-fda-p110015.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p080025.title: Sacral neuromodulation for fecal incontinence
source-fda-p080025.purpose: A sacral-nerve stimulation therapy originally indicated for chronic fecal incontinence in patients who failed or could not tolerate conservative treatment.
source-fda-p080025.relevance: The relevant function is bowel continence. This clinical association does not place the electrodes in the colon or rectal wall.
source-fda-p080025.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100014.title: Injectable treatment for fecal incontinence
source-fda-p100014.purpose: An injectable gel for fecal incontinence in adults who have failed conservative approaches such as dietary, fiber or anti-motility therapy, under the original indication.
source-fda-p100014.relevance: The entry concerns bowel continence. The indexed approval does not by itself establish a precise injection coordinate on this body model.
source-fda-p100014.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p040027.title: Portosystemic shunting for portal hypertension
source-fda-p040027.purpose: An endoprosthesis for de novo or revision treatment of portal hypertension and complications including variceal bleeding, gastropathy, ascites or hepatic hydrothorax.
source-fda-p040027.relevance: The intervention concerns the liver’s portal circulation. A complication elsewhere in the body does not make that site the implant target.
source-fda-p040027.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p200029.title: Internal radiation treatment of liver cancer
source-fda-p200029.purpose: Selective internal radiation therapy for local control of specified solitary unresectable hepatocellular tumors. The original approval defines tumor size, liver function and performance-status requirements.
source-fda-p200029.relevance: The treatment target is hepatocellular carcinoma in the liver. This does not establish treatment of every liver tumor or a general cancer cure.
source-fda-p200029.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p200031.title: Preserving and assessing a donor liver
source-fda-p200031.purpose: An extracorporeal perfusion and monitoring system that preserves donor livers and allows ex-vivo assessment of hemodynamic and metabolic function, subject to the original donor-selection criteria.
source-fda-p200031.relevance: The system works on a donor liver outside the body. It is not a liver implant or proof that a particular organ is suitable for transplantation.
source-fda-p200031.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p990065.title: Liver-directed treatment of colorectal metastases
source-fda-p990065.purpose: Originally indicated for unresectable liver metastases from colorectal cancer in combination with intra-hepatic-artery chemotherapy using floxuridine.
source-fda-p990065.relevance: The treated tumors are in the liver. Colorectal describes the primary cancer’s origin, not a delivery site in the colon.
source-fda-p990065.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p060006.title: Stenting a narrowed renal artery
source-fda-p060006.purpose: An adjunct to renal angioplasty to help maintain patency in specified short atherosclerotic renal-artery lesions near the aorta, within the original vessel-size criteria.
source-fda-p060006.relevance: The physical vessel is the renal artery supplying the kidney. This is not a stent implanted in kidney parenchyma.
source-fda-p060006.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p220023.title: Ultrasound renal denervation for hypertension
source-fda-p220023.purpose: An adjunctive blood-pressure treatment for hypertension inadequately controlled by lifestyle changes and antihypertensive medication, using an ultrasound renal-denervation system.
source-fda-p220023.relevance: The relevant system is the renal vascular and neural pathway. This is not evidence of measuring kidney filtration or placing electrodes inside kidney tissue.
source-fda-p220023.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p170001.title: Sacral neuromodulation for urinary symptoms
source-fda-p170001.purpose: Treats urinary retention and overactive-bladder symptoms in patients who failed or could not tolerate conservative approaches, under the original indication.
source-fda-p170001.relevance: The physiological function is bladder control. Sacral neuromodulation does not imply implantation of the stimulator inside the bladder.
source-fda-p170001.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p050027.title: Blue-light detection of bladder lesions
source-fda-p050027.product: Karl Storz D-Light C PDD system
source-fda-p050027.purpose: Used with Cysview as an adjunct to white-light cystoscopy to detect non-muscle-invasive papillary bladder cancer in specified suspected or known-lesion patients.
source-fda-p050027.relevance: The inspected organ is the bladder. This is an optical detection aid used with a drug, not a cancer-ablation device.
source-fda-p050027.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p170023.title: Urethral bulking for stress incontinence
source-fda-p170023.purpose: A urethral injection treatment for adult women with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency, including stress-predominant mixed incontinence, under the original indication.
source-fda-p170023.relevance: The source identifies urethral injection. This is distinct from an implanted bladder stimulator and from treatment of urinary infection.
source-fda-p170023.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p210020.title: Drug-coated balloon treatment of urethral narrowing
source-fda-p210020.purpose: Treats obstructive urinary symptoms associated with anterior urethral strictures of no more than 3 cm in adult men, under the original indication.
source-fda-p210020.relevance: The treated structure is the anterior urethra. The BPH catheter system has a different application and is not merged with this entry.
source-fda-p210020.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010055.title: Microwave thermotherapy for enlarged prostate symptoms
source-fda-p010055.purpose: A minimally invasive microwave-thermotherapy system for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia. The original approval specifies prostate size and prostatic-urethral length requirements.
source-fda-p010055.relevance: The condition is enlargement of the prostate. The urethral length is a treatment-selection measurement, not evidence of a separate urethral implant.
source-fda-p010055.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p060010.title: Temporary urine-flow support after BPH treatment
source-fda-p060010.purpose: A temporary stent, originally for up to 30 days, to maintain urine flow and allow voluntary urination after minimally invasive BPH treatment and initial catheterization.
source-fda-p060010.relevance: The supported passage is in the prostatic urinary outlet. This is not a permanent prostate replacement or a treatment for prostate cancer.
source-fda-p060010.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000006.title: Penile prosthesis for erectile dysfunction
source-fda-p000006.product: Mentor Alpha I penile prosthesis, P000006
source-fda-p000006.purpose: A penile prosthesis for men with erectile dysfunction who are considered candidates for implantation, under the original approval statement.
source-fda-p000006.relevance: The intended intervention is penile implantation. The original statement names Alpha I while the database title now names Titan; this entry does not assume those historical product identities are interchangeable.
source-fda-p000006.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000040.title: Endometrial ablation for excessive bleeding
source-fda-p000040.purpose: Ablates the uterine lining in premenopausal women with excessive bleeding from benign causes who have completed childbearing, under the original indication.
source-fda-p000040.relevance: The treated tissue is the endometrium within the uterus. It is not an intervention for preserving future fertility.
source-fda-p000040.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p040003.title: Focused-ultrasound ablation of uterine fibroids
source-fda-p040003.purpose: An MR-guided focused-ultrasound ablation system for symptomatic uterine fibroids in selected pre- or perimenopausal women who have completed childbearing and meet the original uterine-size criterion.
source-fda-p040003.relevance: The target is fibroid tissue in the uterus. This application is separate from ExAblate neurotechnology used at intracranial targets.
source-fda-p040003.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p240015.title: Reducing recurrence of intrauterine adhesions
source-fda-p240015.purpose: Intended to reduce recurrence and severity of postsurgical adhesions inside the uterus after hysteroscopic surgery for symptomatic moderate-to-severe intrauterine adhesions in adult women.
source-fda-p240015.relevance: The source explicitly identifies the uterine cavity. Female anatomy is listed textually and is not falsely placed on the male reference mesh.
source-fda-p240015.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-k260007.title: Vaginal moisturization and lubrication
source-fda-k260007.purpose: Vaginal lubricant suppositories intended to supplement natural lubrication and improve comfort during intimate activity. The FDA summary states that the product is not compatible with condoms.
source-fda-k260007.relevance: The source identifies vaginal application and mucosal contact. This is not a contraceptive, despite the regulatory category’s name, and it is not placed on the male reference mesh.
source-fda-k260007.locator: FDA 510(k) summary, PDF page 5; indications for use

source-fda-p020056.title: Breast augmentation and reconstruction
source-fda-p020056.purpose: Silicone-filled implants originally indicated for augmentation in women aged 22 or older and reconstruction in women of any age, including specified revision procedures.
source-fda-p020056.relevance: The intervention concerns breast volume and reconstruction. The application’s later Natrelle title does not establish that every later model shares this original labeling.
source-fda-p020056.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p080003.title: Digital breast imaging and tomosynthesis
source-fda-p080003.purpose: Generates 2D and 3D mammographic images for breast-cancer screening and diagnostic workup, under the original system indication.
source-fda-p080003.relevance: The imaged anatomy is the breast. This is external imaging, not a breast implant or proof of a cancer diagnosis from an image alone.
source-fda-p080003.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p110006.title: Supplemental ultrasound screening in dense breasts
source-fda-p110006.purpose: An adjunct to mammography for specified asymptomatic women with dense breasts and normal or benign mammograms, without prior clinical breast intervention, under the original indication.
source-fda-p110006.relevance: The measured tissue is breast parenchyma. The source describes supplemental screening, not replacement of mammography for all patients.
source-fda-p110006.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p050052.title: Subdermal filling of facial folds
source-fda-p050052.purpose: Originally indicated for subdermal implantation to correct moderate to severe facial wrinkles and folds, such as nasolabial folds.
source-fda-p050052.relevance: The specified tissue layer is beneath the dermis. This skin-region association is not a claim about implantation in muscle, bone or brain.
source-fda-p050052.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000013.title: Primary total hip arthroplasty
source-fda-p000013.purpose: Hip-replacement systems for patients requiring primary total hip arthroplasty because of specified painful, disabling non-inflammatory degenerative hip disease.
source-fda-p000013.relevance: The replaced joint is the hip. This application does not establish eligibility for every revision procedure or every later component model.
source-fda-p000013.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p040033.title: Resurfacing the hip joint
source-fda-p040033.purpose: A hip-resurfacing system for specified arthritic conditions. The original design combines a cemented femoral-head component with a cementless acetabular component and has patient-selection restrictions.
source-fda-p040033.relevance: Both components belong to the hip joint. This historical resurfacing indication is not evidence of superiority over total hip replacement.
source-fda-p040033.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010014.title: Partial replacement of the medial knee compartment
source-fda-p010014.purpose: A cemented partial-knee implant for osteoarthritis or avascular necrosis limited to the medial compartment, under the original indication.
source-fda-p010014.relevance: The treated structure is the medial knee compartment. It is not replacement of the whole knee or a vascular intervention above the knee.
source-fda-p010014.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p010029.title: Hyaluronate treatment for knee osteoarthritis pain
source-fda-p010029.purpose: A sodium-hyaluronate treatment originally indicated for knee osteoarthritis pain after inadequate response to conservative non-drug therapy and simple analgesics.
source-fda-p010029.relevance: The clinical target is knee osteoarthritis pain. The original approval names Nuflexxa; the current database title uses Euflexxa, so the naming difference remains explicit.
source-fda-p010029.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p060037.title: Cemented mobile-bearing knee replacement
source-fda-p060037.purpose: Knee-replacement components for severe knee pain and disability associated with specified arthritic conditions or deformities. The original approval specifies cemented use.
source-fda-p060037.relevance: The intervention is at the knee joint. The source limits deformity and disease criteria; it is not a general treatment for all knee pain.
source-fda-p060037.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-k260721.title: Glenoid replacement in shoulder arthroplasty
source-fda-k260721.purpose: A cemented glenoid implant for severe pain or disability from degenerative shoulder disease, or qualifying revision surgery with sufficient bone stock. Compatible humeral-system indications also apply.
source-fda-k260721.relevance: The glenoid is the shoulder socket. This is an implant component used with specified humeral systems, not a whole-joint replacement independent of component compatibility.
source-fda-k260721.locator: FDA 510(k) summary, PDF page 4; indications for use

source-fda-p000057.title: Replacement of damaged finger knuckle joints
source-fda-p000057.purpose: Total replacement of specified finger metacarpophalangeal joints affected by painful, destructive or degenerative disease, where soft-tissue reconstruction can provide adequate stabilization.
source-fda-p000057.relevance: The source identifies finger MCP joints. This is not a wrist replacement, elbow implant or tendon repair.
source-fda-p000057.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p950035.title: Electrical assistance for grasp and release
source-fda-p950035.purpose: An upper-extremity neuroprosthesis intended to improve grasp, hold and release in selected skeletally mature people with C5 or C6 spinal-cord injury and preserved lower-motor-neuron innervation of the forearm and hand.
source-fda-p950035.relevance: The assisted function is hand grasp. Spinal-cord injury describes the clinical population; the source does not place this system’s electrodes inside the spinal cord.
source-fda-p950035.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p960053.title: Thumb-base joint replacement
source-fda-p960053.purpose: A total-joint replacement for skeletally mature patients with pain or instability of the thumb’s trapezometacarpal joint from specified disease, trauma or prior procedures.
source-fda-p960053.relevance: The relevant joint is at the base of the thumb. It should not be displayed as a replacement of all fingers or of the wrist as a whole.
source-fda-p960053.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p050050.title: Non-cemented ankle replacement
source-fda-p050050.purpose: A non-cemented implant to replace a painful arthritic ankle joint affected by osteoarthritis, post-traumatic arthritis or rheumatoid arthritis, under the original indication.
source-fda-p050050.relevance: The replaced joint is the ankle. This is not an implant in the knee or a treatment of the plantar fascia.
source-fda-p050050.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100006.title: Graft material for ankle or hindfoot fusion
source-fda-p100006.purpose: An alternative to autograft in specified ankle or hindfoot fusion procedures when supplemental graft material is needed, under the original disease and surgical criteria.
source-fda-p100006.relevance: The source identifies ankle and hindfoot arthrodesis. Fusion and joint replacement are different interventions; this is not a motion-preserving ankle prosthesis.
source-fda-p100006.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p040026.title: External shock-wave treatment for chronic heel pain
source-fda-p040026.purpose: A non-invasive treatment for proximal plantar fasciitis in adults with symptoms lasting at least six months despite unsuccessful conservative therapy, under the original indication.
source-fda-p040026.relevance: The target is the plantar-fascia insertion at the heel. The energy is applied externally; the entry does not imply an implanted heel device.
source-fda-p040026.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p000058.title: Bone-graft and cage system for lumbar fusion
source-fda-p000058.purpose: A spinal-fusion system originally indicated for skeletally mature patients with specified single-level L4–S1 degenerative disc disease after at least six months of nonoperative treatment.
source-fda-p000058.relevance: The structural target is the lumbar vertebral segment. The device is not implanted in spinal-cord tissue, and this original combination does not represent every later INFUSE use.
source-fda-p000058.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p060023.title: Cervical disc reconstruction after discectomy
source-fda-p060023.purpose: A cervical disc prosthesis for selected skeletally mature patients undergoing single-level C3–C7 discectomy for intractable radiculopathy or myelopathy after failed nonoperative treatment.
source-fda-p060023.relevance: The reconstructed structure is an intervertebral disc in the neck. Spinal-cord symptoms do not mean that the prosthesis contacts or penetrates the cord.
source-fda-p060023.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p140019.title: Bone-graft support for cervical reconstruction
source-fda-p140019.purpose: A graft for specified single-level cervical reconstruction after failed conservative care. The original approval requires use inside an allograft bone ring with supplemental anterior plate fixation.
source-fda-p140019.relevance: The relevant anatomy is the cervical disc space and supporting vertebrae. This is not a stand-alone implant for spinal-cord stimulation.
source-fda-p140019.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p030004.title: Embolization before brain AVM surgery
source-fda-p030004.purpose: Originally indicated for presurgical embolization of brain arteriovenous malformations.
source-fda-p030004.relevance: The intervention is in abnormal brain blood vessels. It is not an electrode, and the regional association does not establish a precise vessel location.
source-fda-p030004.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100018.title: Endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms
source-fda-p100018.purpose: Originally indicated for adults aged 22 or older with large or giant wide-necked intracranial aneurysms in specified internal-carotid segments.
source-fda-p100018.relevance: The source identifies intracranial vasculature. This entry is kept in the brain region rather than implying a target at the neck carotid landmark.
source-fda-p100018.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p100034.title: Electric-field treatment of recurrent glioblastoma
source-fda-p100034.purpose: Originally indicated as monotherapy for recurrent supratentorial glioblastoma in adults aged 22 or older after chemotherapy, when surgical and radiation options had been exhausted.
source-fda-p100034.relevance: The intended disease target is in the brain. This original approval does not establish the device’s later indications or a general treatment for every brain tumor.
source-fda-p100034.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p210007.title: Vagus stimulation paired with stroke rehabilitation
source-fda-p210007.purpose: Stimulates the vagus nerve during rehabilitation therapy to address upper-extremity motor deficits in chronic ischemic-stroke patients with moderate to severe arm impairment, under the original indication.
source-fda-p210007.relevance: The stimulated structure is the vagus nerve. Stroke is the disease context, not evidence of an electrode implanted in the infarcted brain region.
source-fda-p210007.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits

source-fda-p130028.title: Spinal cord stimulation for chronic intractable pain
source-fda-p130028.purpose: An aid in managing chronic intractable trunk or limb pain, including specified pain associated with failed-back-surgery syndrome, under the original indication.
source-fda-p130028.relevance: The system is identified as spinal cord stimulation. The indexed approval does not by itself establish lead position, penetration of cord tissue or comparative effectiveness.
source-fda-p130028.locator: Original FDA approval order statement; historical indication and eligibility limits
